beats.say: Soldiers said a giant desert spider would chase you down, and scream.
A photo went around of ones so big, they looked like dinner plates.
The camel spider. And it isn't even a spider. It's a solpugid.
Venomous? No. It has no venom at all.
That photo was a trick. Held close to the camera, they looked eight to ten times bigger.
And chasing you? It's running for your shade.
It doesn't eat camels, or people. Only small animals.
The biggest bodies are about five centimeters, two inches.
Fast? The only measured speeds were under one mile an hour.
Scream? Some can make a tiny buzz or hiss.
The legend is over two hundred years old in Arab countries.
Americans first heard it from Gulf War veterans.
Nobody has ever named a real victim. It always happened to a friend.
It lays its eggs in the soil, not under a camel's skin.
Even the highest speed scientists mention is about ten miles an hour.
It's a desert hunter, of creatures smaller than itself.
That viral photo was emailed around in two thousand four.
Would you still sleep in that desert tent?
